fact_rationales.F11: Bilateral inferior lens dislocation is a characteristic feature of Marfan syndrome and Homocystinuria, but less common in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Loeys-Dietz syndrome.
fact_rationales.F12: Long slender fingers are a common feature of Marfan syndrome, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and Loeys-Dietz syndrome, but also present in Homocystinuria, making it a less specific finding.

fact_rationales.F14: Hyperelastic skin is a characteristic feature of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
fact_rationales.F15: Thumb and fifth finger overlap is a feature of Marfan syndrome and Loeys-Dietz syndrome.
fact_rationales.F8: Height above the 99th percentile is more commonly seen in Marfan syndrome and Loeys-Dietz syndrome.
